name: Little Women
hook: Four sisters, one 1868 bestseller, and the March family Jeopardy never stops asking about.

facts.label: Louisa May Alcott
facts.statement: Louisa May Alcott published Little Women in 1868, modeling Jo on herself and three sisters on her own siblings; sister Elizabeth, dead at 22, was the model for Beth.

facts.label: Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy
facts.statement: The four March sisters are Meg (Margaret), Jo, Beth and Amy; Meg complains, 'It's so dreadful to be poor.'

facts.label: Jo March
facts.statement: Jo is the second-oldest, the tomboy of the family, and Alcott's stand-in; she becomes a writer and marries Professor Bhaer.

facts.label: Beth March
facts.statement: Beth is the shy, timid sister nicknamed 'Little Tranquillity' who dies young, as did the real Elizabeth Alcott at 22.

facts.label: Amy March
facts.statement: Amy is the youngest sister, 'a most important person, in her own opinion at least'; her name means 'loved,' and she marries Laurie.

facts.label: Little Men
facts.statement: Little Men is subtitled 'Life at Plumfield with Jo's Boys'; Good Wives, published in 1869, was the earlier follow-up.

facts.label: the Civil War
facts.statement: The girls' father, Mr. March, is an army chaplain serving in the Civil War, which keeps him away from home.
